{{short description|German scientist}}
'''Inge Schmitz-Feuerhake''' (born in [[Osnabrück, Germany]] on 28 September 1935) is a German physicist and mathematician. Her research has assessed the biological effects of [[ionizing radiation]] at low dosage levels.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.2307/3431710 |vauthors=Hoffmann W, Kranefeld A, Schmitz-Feuerhake I |title=Radium-226-contaminated drinking water: hypothesis on an exposure pathway in a population with elevated childhood leukemia |journal=Environmental Health Perspectives |volume=101 |issue=Suppl 3 |pages=113–5 |date=October 1993 |pmid=8143601 |pmc=1521172 |publisher=Brogan |jstor=3431710}}</ref> From 1973 and until her retirement in 2000 she was a professor in experimental physics at the [[University of Bremen]]. Much of her research concerned the  areas of [[radiation contamination]] and the effect of [[Linear no-threshold model|low level radiation]] exposure, as well as the diagnostic use of nuclear radiation.<ref name="tschernobylkongress">[http://www.tschernobylkongress.de/referentinnen/artikel/f241eba6fdc944a8bff86ea6bebfa14b/prof-dr-rer-nat-inge-schmitz-feu.html Prof. Dr. rer. nat. Inge Schmitz-Feuerhake] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120426005104/http://www.tschernobylkongress.de/referentinnen/artikel/f241eba6fdc944a8bff86ea6bebfa14b/prof-dr-rer-nat-inge-schmitz-feu.html |date=2012-04-26 }}, IPPNW (German language). Download 27-Nov-2011.</ref>

==Career==
Her work made a major contribution to the development of biological [[dosimetry]] methods in which changes to the chromosomes in [[white blood cell]]s are measured with extreme precision, by making it possible to count the concerned white blood cells under the microscope.<ref name="strahlentelex">[http://www.strahlentelex.de/Stx_03_404_S06-07.pdf Nuclear-Free Future Award für Inge Schmitz-Feuerhake], [[:de:Strahlentelex]] Nr. 404-405, 2003 (p. 6). Download 27-Nov-2011.</ref>

She wrote of her scientific findings in comprehensible language, so that they can be understood by colleagues from related disciplines and interested laypeople.<ref name="nuclearfree">[http://www.nuclear-free.com/english/ingrid.htm Dr. Inge Schmitz-Feuerhake] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071029035536/http://www.nuclear-free.com/english/ingrid.htm |date=2007-10-29 }}</ref>{{Unreliable source?|date=June 2010}}

Recently, she put forward arguments against the use of [[mammography]] as [[breast cancer screening]]. Her analysis showed that precisely those women who [[Cancer Family syndrome|inherited a higher risk of developing breast cancer]] were put at undue risk due to the radiation absorbed during the screening. Her work was praised by the medical associations of several German states.<ref name="strahlentelex"/>

Schmitz-Feuerhake became known in Germany for examining the rise of the number of children suffering [[leukemia]] in the surroundings of the [[Krümmel Nuclear Power Plant]]. In 1980 she examined dust in the attics of private houses in [[Elbmarsch]] and found an amount of [[plutonium]] that was not explainable by the [[Chernobyl disaster]] nor by [[nuclear weapons testing]] in the 1960s. According to her, she could prove that the found plutonium and nuclear fission products had their origin in the nuclear reactor of Krümmel.{{Citation needed|date=June 2010}} She became known as “the most well-known and likely most relentless anti-nuclear activist” against the [[cancer cluster]] [[Elbmarsch#Cancer cluster|Elbmarsch]].<ref>''Die prominenteste und wohl auch hartnäckigste Anti-Atomkraft-Aktivistin ist die Physikerin Inge Schmitz-Feuerhake.'' (''The most prominent and likely most relentless anti-nuclear activist is the physicist Inge Schmitz-Feuerhake.''). Cited from: ''Inhalt: Sendung vom 10. Dezember 1998. Krebskranke Kinder beim Kernkraftwerk Krümmel - Das Desaster der Atomkritiker'', [[Das Erste]]. Download 27-Nov-2011.</ref>

In 2003 Schmitz-Feuerhake received the [[Nuclear-Free Future Award]] for her lifetime achievement.<ref name="strahlentelex"/><ref name="nuclearfree"/>
She is also chairman of the [[European Committee on Radiation Risk]],<ref name="tschernobylkongress"/> a group of scientists opposing nuclear power; she was elected chairman in 2003.{{Citation needed|date=June 2010}}

Schmitze-Feuerhake is vice president of Gesellschaft für Strahlenschutz e.V. (German Society for Radiation Protection).<ref>"[http://weltderwunder.de.msn.com/technik-und-weltraum-article.aspx?cp-documentid=156669412 „Wir haben es jetzt mit dem Super-GAU zu tun“ – deutsche Experten vergleichen Fukushima mit Tschernobyl] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120323121843/http://weltderwunder.de.msn.com/technik-und-weltraum-article.aspx?cp-documentid=156669412 |date=2012-03-23 }}", http://weltderwunder.de.msn.com {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110714130004/http://weltderwunder.de.msn.com/ |date=2011-07-14 }}, 24 March 2011, retrieved 2011-07-11</ref>
